pk.context: 40 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: white to light yellow, oblong, film-coated tablet

tell: Its 79-hour terminal half-life, and a meal that cuts peak concentration by almost half, set this PA endonuclease inhibitor apart.

clues.text: Nearly all of an oral dose is converted to the active form. A meal lowers peak concentration by 48%, protein binding is 92.9% to 93.9%, and feces carry 80.1% of the dose.
The molecular mass is 571.55 grams per mole, and it is practically insoluble in water.
Approved under an NDA as 40 mg and 80 mg tablets, and as 30 mg and 40 mg granule packets; a single oral dose set by body weight.
No boxed warning. Contraindicated after any prior hypersensitivity to the drug or its ingredients; anaphylaxis and angioedema are among the serious allergic reactions.
Treatment of acute uncomplicated influenza in patients 5 years and older symptomatic for no more than 48 hours, and post-exposure prophylaxis of influenza in patients 5 years and older.
It inhibits the influenza virus polymerase acidic (PA) endonuclease, an enzyme the virus needs, and acts as an antiviral against influenza virus.
The generic name begins with B and has seventeen letters in two words.
